name: Tapestry, Inc.
executive_summary: Tapestry, Inc. (TPR) is a US-listed accessible-luxury house (~86% Coach, ~13% Kate Spade after the Stuart Weitzman divestiture) that the quantitative screen rates as a **buy** on cash generation, quality, and dividend characteristics rather than classic deep value. Fiscal 2026 net sales reached **$8.0bn** (+14% year on year), driven by Coach (+24%) while Kate Spade continued to contract (-10%). The valuation hook is mid-teens earnings against ~**6% FCF yield** and a Piotroski score of **8/9**, but elevated **P/B (33.5×)** and leverage screens flag balance-sheet and capital-structure risk. The central debate is whether Coach’s momentum and the “Amplify” 2028 strategy justify the multiple, or whether Kate Spade weakness, tariffs, and intensifying competition cap rerating.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s buy signal (8/22 models; composite **52%**, sector-relative **58%**) rests on four of five factor families: **cheapness, quality, dividend, and risk**. TPR passes FCF Yield, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Piotroski F-Score, and Earnings Quality — a profile consistent with a cash-rich brand owner rather than a Graham-style net-net.

Business quality aligns with those passes. Coach delivered **$6.9bn** of fiscal 2026 segment net sales (+24% vs fiscal 2025’s **$5.6bn**), handbags and accessories gained share within the portfolio, and nine-month fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was **$1.46bn** vs **$770m** in the prior-year period (10-Q). Management is concentrating the portfolio (Stuart Weitzman sold 4 August 2025 for **~$109m**) and launched the **Amplify** 2028 growth framework in fiscal 2026, targeting Gen Z acquisition and margin expansion.

For a value investor, the case is not asset-based cheapness — Graham, Schloss, and Deep Value models fail on P/B and EV metrics — but **normalised earnings power vs price**: fiscal 2026 diluted EPS of **$7.27** (Yahoo fallback; see Financial Review) on ~**$1.8bn** FCF implies the market is not fully pricing sustained Coach-led cash conversion, particularly after the post-earnings selloff in August 2025. Dividend growth model passage and **1.6% yield** add a shareholder-return floor, though buybacks (**$1.25bn** repurchased in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 per 10-Q) are the dominant capital-return lever.
financial_review:
**Primary source coverage:** Three annual 10-Ks (FY2024–FY2026) and six interim 10-Qs are indexed with body extracts. Segment net-sales tables are available in the FY2026 and FY2025 10-K extracts; consolidated income statements for FY2026/FY2025 annual periods are **not present** in the truncated 10-K bodies — interim 10-Q statements and Yahoo annual data are used where noted.

**Annual revenue trend (filings — segment/product table, FY2026 10-K):**

| Fiscal year | Total net sales | Coach | Kate Spade | Stuart Weitzman |
|-------------|-----------------|-------|------------|-----------------|
| FY2026 (to 27 Jun 2026) | **$8,004.2m** | $6,914.7m | $1,074.9m | $14.6m (pre-sale) |
| FY2025 (to 28 Jun 2025) | **$7,010.7m** | $5,598.5m | $1,197.1m | $215.1m |
| FY2024 (to 29 Jun 2024) | **$6,671.2m** | $5,095.3m | $1,334.4m | $241.5m |

Year-on-year group sales growth: **+14%** (FY26 vs FY25) and **+5%** (FY25 vs FY24). Coach grew **+23%** in FY26; Kate Spade declined **-10%** for a third consecutive year of brand-level contraction.

**Profitability and earnings (Yahoo fallback — consolidated P&L absent from annual filing extracts):**

| | FY2026 | FY2025 | FY2024 |
|--|--------|--------|--------|
| Operating income | **$1,914m** | $1,270m* | $1,140m |
| Net income | **$1,528m** | $183m | $816m |
| Diluted EPS | **$7.27** | $0.82 | $3.50 |
| Free cash flow | **$1,813m** | $1,094m | $1,147m |

\*FY2025 net income was depressed by **$975m** of unusual charges, including **$855m** asset impairment (Yahoo; not located in available filing body extracts). This distorts year-on-year GAAP comparisons and screen ROE (headline **2.0%** vs normalised fiscal 2026 profitability).

**Interim momentum (filings — consolidated 10-Q statements):**

- **Q1 FY2026** (to 27 Sep 2025): net sales **$1,704.6m** (+13% vs $1,507.5m); net income **$274.8m**; diluted EPS **$1.28**.
- **Q2 FY2026** (to 27 Dec 2025): net sales **$2,502.4m** (+14%); net income **$561.3m**; diluted EPS **$2.68**.
- **Q3 FY2026** (to 28 Mar 2026): net sales **$1,920.6m** (+21%); net income **$343.8m**; diluted EPS **$1.65**.
- **Nine months FY2026:** net sales **$6,127.6m** (+16%); operating income **$1,472.1m** (+47%); net income **$1,179.9m**; diluted EPS **$5.58** vs **$3.12** prior year.

Implied Q4 FY2026 net sales ~**$1.9bn** (annual minus nine-month total), consistent with Yahoo quarterly revenue of **$1,876.6m**.

**Cash flow and capital allocation (filings):** Nine-month FY2026 operating cash flow **$1,456.3m**; share repurchases **$1,251.9m**; dividends paid **$245.6m** (10-Q). Yahoo full-year FY2026 FCF **$1,813m** and capex **$166m** (fallback). Marketing investment rose to **$962.5m** (12% of net sales) in FY2026 vs **$744.5m** in FY25 (10-K).

**Balance sheet (Q3 FY2026 10-Q, 28 Mar 2026):** cash **$1,046.5m**; long-term debt **$2,377.1m**; stockholders’ equity **$682.4m**; goodwill **$960.4m**. Yahoo FY2026 year-end shows total debt **$3,953m** (including **$1,574m** capital lease obligations) and tangible book value **negative $982m** — explaining Financial Health model failure and extreme reported debt/equity (**572%** on screen inputs).

**Gaps:** Consolidated annual income statements and cash-flow statements for FY2026/FY2025 are missing from 10-K body extracts (truncated before Item 8 tables). FY2025 impairment charge detail not confirmed in available extracts. No going-concern language found in indexed filing bodies.
risks_and_flags:
**Tariffs and trade policy.** The FY2026 10-K devotes extensive risk disclosure to US import duties, IEEPA tariff uncertainty, and Section 122 surcharges; management received **$2m** of IEEPA tariff refunds in FY2026 but warns mitigation may be costly and ineffective. This is a direct margin and inventory-cost risk for Vietnam/Cambodia/Philippines/Bangladesh sourcing.

**Brand concentration and Kate Spade.** Coach is **86.4%** of net sales (10-K). Kate Spade net sales fell to **$1,075m** (-10% YoY) with prior-year goodwill/intangible impairment history ($211m accumulated goodwill impairment per earlier 10-Q notes). Failure to stabilise Kate Spade would limit group margin targets under Amplify.

**Leverage and capital structure.** Long-term debt of **$2.4bn** against equity of **$682m** (Mar 2026 10-Q), plus **$1.6bn** of capital lease obligations (Yahoo), drives screen Financial Health failure. Covenants under debt facilities restrict indebtedness, liens, and restricted payments (10-Q); management states compliance, but low equity amplifies perceived leverage.

**Competitive pressure.** News flow highlights Gap hiring former Coach creative director Reed Krakoff for a handbag line (1 Sep 2025, Yahoo Finance) and Shein’s scale in global fashion (1 Sep 2025) — threats to accessible-luxury share not captured by quantitative screens.

**Execution and guidance risk.** Despite Q4 FY2025 earnings beats, the stock sold off sharply on forward guidance (13–14 Aug 2025 headlines). Fiscal 2027 outlook balances margin expansion against tariff headwinds and Kate Spade losses (28 Aug 2025, Yahoo Finance).

**Governance / insider activity.** Multiple September 2026 reports of officer share sales after option exercises (e.g. CPO Denise Kulikowsky, 10 Sep 2025, MarketBeat/Stock Titan) — routine but worth monitoring alongside heavy buybacks.

**Accounting.** FY2025 impairment-driven GAAP earnings collapse complicates trend analysis; no going-concern flag identified.

**Divestiture.** Stuart Weitzman sale completed 4 August 2025 for **$109m** with a final loss of **$22m** (10-Q) — immaterial financially but removes diversification.

RiskTags: cyclical, competitive, leverage, regulatory, accounting, key_person
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **moderate-to-good** on earnings and strategy, thin on sell-side depth, and heavy on price-movement articles.

**Earnings and guidance (Aug 2025):** “Tapestry (TPR) Tops Q4 Earnings Estimates” and “Posts Q2 CY2026 Sales In Line With Estimates But Stock Drops On Weak Guidance” (13 Aug 2025, Yahoo Finance); “Tapestry Crushed Earnings but the Stock Plunged” (14 Aug 2025); “Why Tapestry (TPR) Shares Are Getting Obliterated Today” (16 Aug 2025). Pattern: beats on profitability, market focused on forward outlook.

**Strategy:** “Tapestry (TPR) Delivers On Its Boldest Promise Early” (21 Aug 2025); “TPR's Fiscal 2027 Outlook Pits Margin Expansion Against Tariff Risk” (28 Aug 2025); “Tapestry's International Growth Accelerates on China & Europe Gains” (8 Sep 2025).

**Competitive landscape:** “Gap taps Coach architect Reed Krakoff for $29.95–$498 handbag line” (1 Sep 2025, Yahoo Finance) — direct Coach competitive read-through.

**Index / flow:** “Tapestry (TPR) Stock Loses Its Place In Several Major Russell Indices” (4 Jul 2025) — potential passive selling overhang.

**Insider / officer sales:** “Tapestry (NYSE: TPR) officer plans to sell over 10,000 shares” (9 Sep 2025); “CPO sells shares after option exercise” (10 Sep 2025).

**Analyst sentiment:** “Barclays and UBS stick with Buy ratings” (10 Sep 2025, ad-hoc-news.de) amid recent volatility.
research_rationale: Deep research largely confirms the screen’s quality-and-FCF buy case via Coach-led fiscal 2026 acceleration, but elevated leverage, Kate Spade deterioration, and tariff/competitive risks prevent full conviction until FY2025 impairment noise clears and forward guidance stabilises.
